title: Prompt Injection in RAG Systems: Does Retrieval Context Bypass Safety More Reliably Than Direct Prompting?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: RAG is one of the most common LLM deployment patterns. If retrieval context has systematically higher injection success than direct prompting, it reveals a critical gap in safety alignment. Directly actionable for deployment teams.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Setting up a simple RAG pipeline (embedding + vector store + retrieval) is feasible with LangChain and Colab Pro. Injecting documents and comparing attack modes is intermediate-level scripting. Requires understanding of RAG architecture.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused comparison: RAG injection vs. direct injection vs. system prompt injection on same tasks. Clear deliverable (ASR comparison table). Can use a minimal RAG setup. Fits in 30 hours if kept to one model.

novelty.reasoning: RAG prompt injection is extensively studied. PoisonedRAG (USENIX Security 2025) demonstrated that 5 malicious documents in a corpus of millions achieves 90% targeted attack success. 'Backdoored Retrievers for Prompt Injection Attacks on RAG' (arXiv:2410.14479) studies retrieval-stage attacks. OWASP ranks prompt injection as the #1 LLM risk for 2025. However, the specific controlled comparison of ASR across three attack vectors (RAG injection vs. direct injection vs. system prompt injection) on the same model and tasks has not been published as a systematic empirical study. The individual attack vectors are well-studied; the head-to-head comparison framing adds incremental novelty.
